turn.user_message: Where do planned admissions come from?
turn.context: Prompt 2 of bm-pr-04 and bm-pr-05. bed-management.md §7.4.2: OPD prescriptions become the intake point for planned-admission data (date, procedure, likely stay, theatre need); the desk confirms back with a tentative bed. The slip is an example.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Processes, turn 6 (the record stops at 31)

text: From the OPD slip. When a doctor advises admission, the slip already holds most of what the bed plan needs.
bullets: Today those details stay on paper in OPD. The bed is found on the day the patient comes.
Written down once, they let the plan hold a bed days ahead. The theatre and insurance can start early too.
When the patient books at the desk, the date is confirmed back. A bed number is attached at once.
chat.invite: Next, we can see who needs to agree to all this.
prompts: Who needs to agree to this?
Who would write this down in OPD?
What if the patient does not come?
chat.pointer: Pick a line of the slip to see what it feeds. Then pull the slip into the bed plan.

blocks.title: The bed plan starts in OPD
blocks.deck: One OPD slip, and what each line gives the bed plan. Pull it across to see.

blocks.slip_sub: An example slip, written in OPD on Tuesday

plan.label: Bed plan · Thursday
plan.title: One planned admission
plan.bed_note: Held for now. Confirmed when the patient books in.

blocks.rule: The details are written once, in OPD. The plan, the theatre and the insurance desk all read the same slip.

sheets.title: Procedure
sheets.text: The procedure tells the plan which ward and which kind of bed.
sheets.entry: Which procedures fill most of your beds?

sheets.title: Admit on
sheets.text: The day lets the bed be held days ahead, not found on the morning.
sheets.entry: How far ahead are admissions booked?

sheets.title: Likely stay
sheets.text: The likely stay tells the plan when this bed will be free for the next patient.
sheets.entry: Do OPD doctors write a likely stay today?

sheets.title: Operation theatre
sheets.text: A theatre slot booked with the bed, so the stay does not start with a wait.

sheets.title: ICU after?
sheets.text: If an ICU bed is needed after the procedure, it is planned with the ward bed.
sheets.entry: How often do planned patients need ICU?

sheets.title: Paid by
sheets.text: Insurance approval can start before the patient arrives, not on the day.
sheets.entry: How long do approvals take here?

blocks.label: Planned admissions with a slip
blocks.sub: Nobody counts this today. Without it, the bed plan has nothing to plan from.
